questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the mobile-first approach in responsive web design?

options.text: Begin styling for mobile devices and scale up

questions.explanation: Mobile‑first means you write CSS targeting small screens first, then add media queries for larger ones.

questions.prompt: Which CSS media query syntax correctly targets viewports wider than 768px?
questions.explanation: min-width includes widths greater than or equal to 768px.

questions.prompt: Why is using percentage widths for container elements advantageous in responsive design?

options.text: Allows elements to scale with viewport

questions.explanation: Percentages make elements adapt to the size of their parent, scaling with the viewport.

questions.prompt: Which CSS property ensures that flex items wrap onto multiple lines when necessary?
questions.explanation: flex-wrap: wrap lets flex items move onto new lines when space runs out.

questions.prompt: The CSS function clamp() can be used to create fluid font sizes that scale between which two values?
questions.explanation: clamp(min, preferred, max) limits a value between a minimum and maximum.

questions.prompt: Which viewport unit is appropriate for setting a height that is 50% of the viewport height?
questions.explanation: vh represents viewport height; 50vh is half the viewport height.
